name.description:
Name of this language runtime; note that it is expected for name to start with implementation language
{@link ImplLanguage#dslName abbreviation). Other elements may be used following the language for custom runtimes.

For example, the "js-browser" runtime has:
 - language: JavaScript
 - location: BROWSER
 - version: ES2015

If type Foo wishes to have a custom implementation for this runtime, it is defined in `Foo.browser.js` instead of
or in addition to `Foo.js`.

languageVersion.description:
The specific version of the {@link ImplLanguage} required to execute {@link Action}s in this runtime.

e.g. language: “JavaScript”, languageVersion: “ES5”
e.g. language: “Python”, languageVersion: “3.6”

runEnvVars.description: Environment variables applied when running an action with an {@link Action.Requirement} with current the runtime

installEnvVars.description: Environment variables applied to the process which installs this runtime

repositories.description:
Usage of the optional `repositories` (ie: locations such as URI/URL) field differs based on the `runtime`.

For Node.js, if `repositories` is defined, it must be an array of length one. The repository will be used by
npm to find and install the `modules`.

For Python `repositories` is defined, those repositories will be searched in precedence is in descending order.

resourceRequirements.description: Resources required to execute {@link Action}s in this runtime

appendLdLibraryPath.description:
If set, append the directory containing this runtime's `lib/` directory to the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment
variable before spawning a new Python process. This is usually required for runtimes that contain CUDA-enabled
ML frameworks (e.g. Tensorflow).

libraries.description:
All libraries required to execute {@link Action}s in this runtime.
Note that if multiple Libraries in this list ultimately provide {@link Library#libraryVersion} for the same
`Library`, then those version specifications must be compatible.
For example, one Library may specify `>=0.10` and another `==0.12` (since `==0.12` can satisfy both of
those requirements).
On the other hand, if one Library specifies `>=0.10`, a second may not specify `==0.9` since that cannot be
resolved.

parents.description: List of parent runtimes for this runtime.

testLibraries.description:
All additional libraries that are required for testing this runtime (but not executing in production)
Note:
   - For Python runtimes, `pytest` will always be installed for testing and therefore does not need to be
     declared here.

title:
An ImplLanguage Runtime specifies a specific {@link ImplLanguage}, a version of the language, a list of
{@link ImplLanguage.Library}, a list of repositories from which to install libraries
(e.g. [conda-forge](https://conda-forge.org/)), and a list of parent Runtimes from which this child runtime inherits
all libraries and repositories.

Some examples:
```ndjson
py-scipy: {name: "py-scipy", language: "python", "languageVersion": "3.9", libraries: ["conda scipy==1.6.2"]}
js-eslint: {name: "js-eslint", language: "JavaScript",  libraries: ["npm @eslint"]} (MyType.js + MyType.eslint.js)
```
name: ImplLanguage.Runtime
